author: reek
body: This is the rung the battery could not reach. codex-vm injects a tick every 55 ms from a host thread whatever the guest programmed, so a guest that programs a timer and then observes a tick has learned nothing -- the tick was coming anyway. The only way to ask the question used to be to take the host's generator out of the picture with CODEX_VM_NO_TIMER, which is not a knob the harness can set, so this ran by hand or not at all.

author: reek
body: What made that necessary was not the host tick but the guest: nothing it could read recorded that any vector had arrived except the two timers. __interrupt_common answers the PIT and the local timer specially and returns from every other vector without leaving a mark, so a delivered interrupt and a dropped one were indistinguishable from inside.

author: reek
body: The handler now records the count and the number of every vector that is NOT a timer, and the timer vectors deliberately do not touch those cells. That is what lets this run in the ordinary battery: the host's periodic tick is vector 32 and cannot appear here, so a count above zero on the line this test programmed is evidence of that line and nothing else.

author: reek
body: The probe routes timer 0 to IOAPIC line 2 and gives that line vector 80, a number no other device in this machine uses. Serial interrupts are never injected and there is no keyboard timeline attached, so vector 80 is the only one that can reach the counter -- and the test demands the recorded vector be exactly 80 rather than merely that something arrived.

author: reek
body: Each turn is a VM exit, which is what lets the host advance its device models and deliver anything it has queued.
